parole.significato: Junior, child, younger person. (Attached to a name, usually one syllable of the given name.)
parole.testo: From Mandarin -兒 /-儿 (-ér).

parole.significato: Used to indicate a tentative suggestion.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 吧 (ba).

parole.significato: A form of the Chinese exercise qigong.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 八段錦／八段锦 (Bā Duàn Jǐn).

parole.significato: The eight trigrams used in Daoist cosmology.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 八卦 (bāguà).

parole.significato: Dahurian angelica
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 白芷 (báizhǐ)

parole.significato: Synonym of bok choy.
parole.testo: From the Pinyin romanization of Mandarin 白菜 (báicài). Doublet of bok choy and pechay.

parole.significato: Vernacular Chinese, as opposed to Classical Chinese
parole.testo: From Mandarin 白話／白话 (báihuà).

parole.significato: A small ethnic group living in Gansu and Sichuan Provinces in China, close to the border with Tibet.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 白馬 /白马 (báimǎ, literally “white horse”).

parole.significato: a Western leftist perceived as condescending or ignorant.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 白左 (báizuǒ, “white left”), derived from 白種人／白种人 (báizhǒngrén, “White person”) + 左派 (zuǒpài, “left-wing”).

parole.significato: A two-stringed bowed string instrument (chordophone) of northern Chinese origin, held vertically, possessing a soundbox…
parole.testo: From Mandarin 板胡 (bǎnhú).

parole.significato: Any of various types of steamed bread or bun used in Chinese cuisine
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 包 (bāo) or Cantonese 包 (baau1). Cognate of Vietnamese bánh bao.

parole.significato: A metal ball held and rotated within the hand to improve manual strength or dexterity or to relax the hand.
parole.testo: Partial calque of Mandarin 保定鐵球 /保定铁球.

parole.significato: Han Chinese who came to Taiwan from mainland China before 1945, often having experienced Japanese rule, as compared to…
parole.testo: From Mandarin 本省人 (běnshěngrén), literally "original province people" (from the point of view that Taiwan is a province of the Republic of China).

parole.significato: A type of jade disk produced in ancient China.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 璧 (bì).

parole.significato: A type of thick noodle from China's Shaanxi province, said to be named for the sound a noodle makes when slapped agains…
parole.testo: Partial calque from Mandarin 𰻞𰻞麵／𰻝𰻝面 (biángbiángmiàn).

parole.significato: Synonym of dazibao.
parole.testo: Calque of Mandarin 大字報 /大字报 (dàzìbào)

parole.significato: Relaxing, chilling.
parole.testo: Phono-semantic matching of Mandarin 冰淇淋 (bīngqílín), itself a partial calque of English ice cream. Originated in a viral video recorded by John Cena in 2021 on Weibo, promoting Fast and Furious 9.

parole.significato: In China, a construction and corporation composed of soldiers, especially working-class ones.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 兵团 (bīngtuán, “army unit, army formation”).

parole.significato: A statue or image of Budai.
parole.testo: Derived from Mandarin 布袋 (Bùdài, “cloth sack”).

parole.significato: choy sum
parole.testo: From Mandarin 菜心 (càixīn, “vegetable heart”). Doublet of choy sum.

parole.significato: grass script (a style of cursive script used in Chinese calligraphy).
parole.testo: From Mandarin 草書／草书 (cǎoshū).

parole.significato: A gambling game played with dice.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 四五六.

parole.significato: A major Chinese school of Mahayana Buddhism characterized by sudden enlightenment achieved by indirect means, developed…
parole.testo: Borrowed from the pinyin romanization of the Mandarin pronunciation of Chinese 禪 /禅 (Chán), a development and clipping of Middle Chinese 禪那 (MC dzyen na), a transcription of Sanskrit ध्यान (dhyāna, literally “meditation”). Doublet of dhyana and Zen.

parole.significato: Any of several minerals discovered by the Chang'e series of lunar landers and Yutu series of lunar rovers
parole.testo: From Chang'e + -s- + -ite. Named after Chinese goddess Chang'e (the moon goddess). Named for the Chang'e program, the Chinese lunar landers which discovered the minerals. From Mandarin Cháng'é (“ㄔㄤˊ ㄜˊ”) (Ch‘ang²-ê²), from Chinese 嫦娥 (Cháng'é).

parole.significato: Synonym of cheongsam (“robe worn by Asian men”).
parole.testo: From Mandarin 長衫／长衫 (chángshān).

parole.significato: A supreme ruler of one or more nomadic tribes of Inner Asian peoples, at some point between the 4th century BCE and the…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 單于 (chányú); ultimately from Xiongnu.

parole.significato: Chinese fried rice.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 炒飯 /炒饭 (chǎofàn), possibly originally from Cantonese 炒飯 /炒饭 (caau² faan⁶). Compare Spanish chaufa, chofán

parole.significato: An East Asian tea bowl, in which tea may be prepared and then consumed.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 茶碗 (cháwǎn) or Japanese 茶碗 (chawan, literally “tea bowl”).

parole.significato: A Chinese person whose name is not known to the speaker.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 陳／陈 (Chén). Doublet of Tan, Chan, and Tran.

parole.significato: An officer of a City Urban Administrative and Law Enforcement Bureau in China.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 城管 (chéngguǎn), short for 城市管理部門 (chéngshì guǎnlǐ bùmén).

parole.significato: A certain kind of Chinese set phrase originating in Classical Chinese, typically four characters in length, and usually…
parole.testo: From Mandarin 成語／成语 (chéngyǔ).

parole.significato: A life force in traditional Chinese philosophy, culture, medicine, etc, related (but not limited) to breath and circula…
parole.testo: From the Mandarin 氣／气 (qì) from the Wade–Giles romanization: chʻi⁴, from Middle Chinese 氣 (MC khj+jH), from Old Chinese 氣 (OC *kʰɯds, “breath, vapor”). Compare modern Japanese 気(き) (ki), Korean 기(氣) (gi) and Vietnamese khí (氣).

parole.significato: The Chinese foot, a traditional Chinese unit of length based on the human forearm.
parole.testo: From the pinyin romanization of Mandarin 尺 (chǐ). Doublet of chek.

parole.significato: A person of perceived Chinese ethnicity or descent.
parole.testo: There are several possible origins of the term: * From the Chinese courtesy ching-ching, a reduplication of Mandarin 請 /请 (qǐng, “please”). Compare chin-chin, Italian cincin, Portuguese tchim-tchim, tim-tim, Spanish chinchín, French tchin-tchin. * From the alteration of China. * From the alteration

parole.significato: A personal comfort item; a small pillow, bolster, blanket or other huggable item retained from one's childhood.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Singaporean Mandarin 臭臭 (chòuchou, literally “smelly (thing)”).

parole.significato: An early Chinese repeating crossbow.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 諸葛弩 /诸葛弩 (Zhūgě nǔ, literally “Zhuge crossbow”) Wade–Giles romanization: chu¹-ko³-nu³.

parole.significato: An early Chinese game somewhat similar to golf.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 捶丸 (chuíwán, literally “ball-hitting”).

parole.significato: One of the Classical Chinese poetry forms
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 詞／词 (cí).

parole.significato: A traditional Chinese snack consisting of cooked glutinous rice pounded into paste.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 糍粑 (cíbā) + cake.

parole.significato: A type of carved jade tube made in China starting in the Neolithic.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 琮 (cóng).

parole.significato: An ancient Chinese ball game involving kicking a ball through an opening into a net.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 蹴鞠 (cùjū).

parole.significato: A large bowed two-stringed chordophone of Chinese origin, a tenor part of the erhu family of instruments.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 大胡 (dàhú).

parole.significato: A business practice in which a person outside of China purchases commodities for a customer in mainland China.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 代購／代购 (dàigòu, “to buy on someone's behalf”).

parole.significato: A Chinese bread based on Russian rye bread, generally available in northeastern China.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 大列巴 (dàlièbā), from 大 (dà, “big”) + 列巴 (lièbā, “bread”, Harbin dialect), the latter from Russian хлеб (xleb, “bread”).

parole.significato: Synonym of picul: a traditional unit of weight and mass, chiefly used as a dry measure of grains.
parole.testo: From the pinyin romanization of the Mandarin pronunciation of Chinese 担 (dàn) and Chinese 石 (dàn).

parole.significato: A genre of Chinese fiction depicting romantic relationships between male characters.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 耽美 (dānměi, “indulging beauty”).

parole.significato: A perennial sage of species Salvia miltiorrhiza, valued in traditional Chinese medicine for its roots.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 丹參／丹参 (dānshēn).

parole.significato: Any of various focal points within the body for the flow of chi energy.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 丹田 (dāntián).

parole.significato: An ethnic minority group found in Southern China and Burma. Languages spoken in regions populated by this group include…
parole.testo: From Mandarin 德昂 (Dé'áng).

parole.significato: A large, bowed Chinese string instrument of the huqin family, with a large soundbox covered at one end with snakeskin.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 低胡 (dīhú).

parole.significato: An ancient Chinese vessel with legs and a lid.
parole.testo: Romanized from Mandarin 鼎 (dǐng).

parole.significato: A priest of the Nakhi people.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 东巴 (dōngbā).

parole.significato: a cultural group of ancient China centered in what is now Shandong province.
parole.testo: From the pinyin romanization of the Mandarin Chinese 東夷 /东夷 (Dōngyí).

parole.significato: A spicy, salty paste made from fermented broad beans, soybeans, salt, rice, and various spices.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 豆瓣醬／豆瓣酱 (dòubànjiàng). Doublet of tobanjan.

parole.significato: Chinese fermented black beans.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 豆豉 (dòuchǐ). Doublet of tousi.

parole.significato: Synonym of dudou.
parole.testo: From the pinyin romanization of Mandarin 兜兜 (dōudōu, “diminutive form of dudou”).

parole.significato: Synonym of dudou.
parole.testo: From the pinyin romanization of Mandarin 兜肚 (dōudù, “literally [item] covering the belly”).

parole.significato: tofu
parole.testo: From the Hanyu Pinyin romanization of the Mandarin pronunciation of Chinese 豆腐 (dòufu). Doublet of tofu and dubu.

parole.significato: A structural element consisting of interlocking wooden brackets as used in traditional Chinese architecture.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 斗拱 (dǒugǒng).

parole.significato: A Chinese dessert made with very soft tofu; tofu pudding.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 豆花 (dòuhuā).

parole.significato: Angelica pubescens
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 獨活 /独活 (dúhuó)

parole.significato: A traditional Chinese female undergarment, usually made of silk, covering the breasts and belly, and tied at the neck a…
parole.testo: From the pinyin romanization of Mandarin 肚兜 (dùdōu, “literally belly cover”).

parole.significato: A governor general, in certain Chinese dynasties.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 都統／都统.

parole.significato: Glue obtained from the skin of the donkey, used as a medicinal ingredient in traditional Chinese medicine.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 阿膠 /阿胶 (ējiāo).

parole.significato: A type of bowed spike fiddle having two strings, originating in China as part of the huqin family of string instruments.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 二胡 (èrhú), from 二 (èr, “two”) + 胡 (hú, “fiddle; short for 胡琴, a family of Chinese vertical fiddles”).

parole.significato: A phonological process that adds rhotic sounds to syllables in some lects of Chinese.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 兒化 /儿化 (érhuà).

parole.significato: Synonym of fat choy.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 髮菜 /发菜 (fàcài).

parole.significato: Synonym of topolect (a regional variety of Chinese)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 方言 (fāngyán).

parole.significato: A kind of receipt that serves as a tax document and sometimes also as a lottery ticket, used in China and Taiwan.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 發票 /发票 (fāpiào).

parole.significato: A system of spiritual energies, both good and evil, present in the natural features of landscapes.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 風水 /风水 (fēngshuǐ, “feng shui (Chinese system of geomancy)”, literally “wind and water”): 風 /风 (fēng, “wind”) + 水 (shuǐ, “water”). Doublet of fung shui.

parole.significato: A phoenix found in Asian mythologies, which reigns over all other birds, often of female sex and frequently found paire…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 鳳凰 /凤凰 (fènghuáng). Doublet of Fung-wong, hoo, and ho-o.

parole.significato: Red panda
parole.testo: Calque from Mandarin 火狐 (huǒhú, literally “fire fox”).

parole.significato: A stylized lion statue similar to those usually placed in male and female pairs outside imperial Chinese palaces, tombs…
parole.testo: Possibly a Western invention, from Mandarin 福 (fú, “good fortune”) + English dog. There is no similar word in Chinese itself that uses the word 福 (fú), but see English foo and Foo. Compare also Chinese 佛 (“Buddha”), pronounced fo or fu in some varieties.

parole.significato: Synonym of Buddha Jumps Over the Wall.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 佛跳墙 (fótiàoqiáng, literally “Buddha Jumps Over the Wall”)

parole.significato: A Chinese literary form developed during the times of the Han dynasty that combines prose and poetry, sometimes called…
parole.testo: From Mandarin 賦／赋 (fù).

parole.significato: The children of the nouveau riche in China.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 富二代 (fù'èrdài, literally “rich second generation”), without syllable-dividing mark (隔音符號／隔音符号 (géyīn fúhào)).

parole.significato: Taoist magic symbols or incantations written or painted on talismans.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 符籙／符箓 (fúlù).

parole.significato: A Chinese lidded cup or bowl, used to steep tea, sometimes including a saucer, developed during the Ming dynasty as an…
parole.testo: From Mandarin 蓋碗 /盖碗 (gàiwǎn, literally “lidded bowl”).

parole.significato: A two-stringed vertical fiddle-like chordophone (stringed instrument) used as a leading instrument in Cantonese music.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 高胡 (gāohú).

parole.significato: A recommended national standard of the People's Republic of China
parole.testo: From Mandarin GB/T, from Mandarin 國標/推薦 /国标/推荐 (guóbiāo/tuījiàn).

parole.significato: A modern Chinese instrument that fuses the Western cello with a more traditional huqin-like design, with four strings t…
parole.testo: From Mandarin 革胡 (géhú).

parole.significato: A kind of boisterous live stage performance taking place during Chinese festivals.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 歌臺 /歌台 (gētái).

parole.significato: A fruit in the genus Lycium, especially in commercial products where it is promoted as a superfruit.
parole.testo: ^((please verify)) A marketing coinage, likely an altered pronunciation of Mandarin 枸杞 (gǒuqǐ). The earliest known usage in print was in a publication in 1996. The first usage in the LexisNexis database is a newspaper article in 2002. Wider usage began in 2003 and 2004.

parole.significato: A kind of cultivation energy, more powerful than qi.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 功 (gōng, “merit; achievement”).

parole.significato: One of the ten "mythical Baidu deities" invented by Chinese internet users for the purpose of circumventing censorship.…
parole.testo: A calque of the Mandarin 草泥馬／草泥马 (cǎonímǎ). See 草泥馬 for more.

parole.significato: A Taiwanese snack food consisting of a slice of stewed meat and other condiments sandwiched between flat steamed bread.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 刈包 (guàbāo), from Hokkien 刈包 (koah-pau).

parole.significato: A treatment used in traditional Chinese medicine involving repeated pressured strokes over the skin with a hard object…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 刮痧 (guāshā, literally “scrape sand”).

parole.significato: A Chinese polearm with the blade mounted on top of the pole (as opposed to on the side like most European polearms).
parole.testo: From Mandarin 關刀 /关刀 (guāndāo, “Guan Yu's halberd”).

parole.significato: Overly enthusiastic or energetic.
parole.testo: From a catachresis of Mandarin 工合 (gōnghé), an acronym for 工業合作社 /工业合作社 (gōngyè hézuòshè, “[Chinese] Industrial Cooperative Society”), as 工 (gōng, “work”) + 合 (“together”), literally “to work together”. The interpretation "work together" was created by U.S. Marine Evans Carlson, who was posted in Ch

parole.significato: A potsticker, a panfried dumpling.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 鍋貼／锅贴 (guōtiē).

parole.significato: A variety of muskmelon from Xinjiang, China, particularly associated with Hami City.
parole.testo: From Hami + melon, calque from Mandarin 哈密瓜 (hāmìguā).

parole.significato: Referring to the largest ethnic group native to China.
parole.testo: From Han (Mandarin 漢 /汉 (Hàn)) + Chinese.

parole.significato: traditional Han Chinese clothing
parole.testo: From Mandarin 漢服 /汉服 (hànfú).

parole.significato: A traitor to China, the Chinese state and, to a lesser extent, Han ethnicity.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 漢奸／汉奸 (hànjiān).

parole.significato: Synonym of red envelope.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Pinyin romanization of Mandarin 紅包 /红包 (hóngbāo), 红包 (hóngbāo, “red envelope, red packet, hongbao”): 紅 /红, 红 (hóng, “red”) + 包 (bāo, “bag, sack; parcel, package”). Doublet of angpao and ang pow.

parole.significato: The imperial Chinese board of revenue, especially its branch in Guangzhou during the Qing Dynasty.
parole.testo: Uncertain, although probably an irregular romanization of the Mandarin pronunciation of Chinese 戶部 /户部 (Hùbù), the imperial government's Board of Revenue which oversaw customs and other taxation during the Qing Dynasty. In reference to its agents, a clipping of earlier hoppo-man.

parole.significato: An administrative subdivision of Taiwan, commonly translated as county. (Alternative form of xian for mainland China.)
parole.testo: From Mandarin 縣 /县 (xiàn), Wade–Giles romanization: hsien⁴.

parole.significato: A type of ceremonial column used in traditional Chinese architecture.
parole.testo: From the pinyin romanization of the Mandarin Chinese pronunciation for 華表／华表 (huábiǎo).

parole.significato: A Chinese medicinal herb (Astragalus membranaceus)
parole.testo: From Mandarin 黃芪 /黄芪 (huángqí), Wade–Giles romanization: Huang²-chʻi².

parole.significato: The Chinese tree Dalbergia odorifera, or the wood of this tree, which is often used in Chinese woodworking.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 黃花梨／黄花梨 (huánghuālí).

parole.significato: A class of Chinese alcoholic beverages made from fermented grains including rice, millet, and wheat, typically 10–20% a…
parole.testo: The atonal pinyin romanization of the Mandarin pronunciation of Chinese 黃酒 /黄酒 (huángjiǔ, “yellow alcohol”). Compare baijiu.

parole.significato: A bacterial infection of citrus trees.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 黃龍病／黄龙病 (huánglóngbìng), literally "yellow dragon disease".

parole.significato: A smartphone made by the Huawei company.
parole.testo: From the company, Huawei. Huawei was borrowed from Mandarin 華為／华为 (Huáwéi). See Wikipedia for more.

parole.significato: An ethnic group of China, distinguished by their practice of Islam, who speak Mandarin (or Dungan in Kyrgyzstan, Kazakh…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 回 (Huí).

parole.significato: A household registration record that identifies a person as a local resident.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 戶口／户口 (hùkǒu).

parole.significato: nine-tailed fox in Chinese mythology
parole.testo: From Mandarin 狐狸精 (húlijīng).

parole.significato: A narrow alley or street in a traditional residential district of a city in China, especially Beijing.
parole.testo: Borrowed from the Hanyu Pinyin romanization of Mandarin 衚衕 /胡同 (hútòng), 胡同 (hútòng, “narrow street”), probably: * from Mongolian гудам (gudam), from Middle Mongol ᠭᠤᠳᠤᠮ (ɣudum, “corridor, passage, passageway”); or * from Mongolian худаг (xudag), ᠬᠤᠳᠳᠤᠭ (qudduɣ, “water well”) (from the prevalence of

parole.significato: Either of two passerine birds of the genus Garrulax, family Leiothrichidae, of mainland China and Taiwan.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 畫眉／画眉 (huàméi, “painted eyebrow”).

parole.significato: A thin Chinese fried-egg pancake similar to a crepe, typically sold as street food.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 煎餅／煎饼 (jiānbǐng). Doublet of senbei.

parole.significato: A reanimated corpse in Chinese legend, which moves around by hopping with its arms outstretched, and kills living creat…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 殭屍／僵尸 (jiāngshī).

parole.significato: A currency unit of the People's Republic of China, one tenth of a yuan.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 角 (jiǎo). Doublet of kak.

parole.significato: The dioecious, herbaceous climbing vine Gynostemma pentaphyllum
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 絞股藍／绞股蓝 (jiǎogǔlán).

parole.significato: A regional military governor in China during the Tang dynasty and the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 節度使 /节度使 (jiédùshǐ) via Hanyu Pinyin.

parole.significato: An ethnic Vietnamese, in reference to those whose lands are in China.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 京 (jīng), as in 京族 (Jīngzú).

parole.significato: Peking opera
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 京劇／京剧 (jīngjù).

parole.significato: Peking opera
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 京戲 /京戏 (jīngxì).

parole.significato: Any Chinese alcoholic beverage
parole.testo: Borrowed from Mandarin 酒 (jiǔ).

parole.significato: Synonym of Ru kiln.
parole.testo: Partial calque of Mandarin 汝窯 /汝窑 (Rǔyáo), using the Wade–Giles romanization of Mandarin 汝 (Rǔ), Ju³, in reference to Ruzhou, where they were located.

parole.significato: Synonym of Ru ware.
parole.testo: Partial calque of Mandarin 汝瓷 (Rǔcí), using the Wade–Giles romanization of Mandarin 汝 (Rǔ), Ju³, in reference to the town of Ruzhou where it was manufactured.

parole.significato: A scroll of a traditional Chinese book, often (but not necessarily) corresponding to a single chapter or fascicle.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 卷.

parole.significato: A sorghum-based variety of baijiu.
parole.testo: From the Wade-Giles romanization of the former pronunciation of Mandarin 高粱 (gāoliáng).

parole.significato: Synonym of Hakka.
parole.testo: From Mandarin 客家 (Kèjiā).

parole.significato: A plucked stringed instrument (chordophone) with a harp-like construction, originating in ancient Chinese music as a ho…
parole.testo: From Mandarin 箜篌 (kōnghóu), from the name of this instrument in the local language of the region of Central Asia whence it came to China; the Sogdian name for the angular harp was [script needed] (cngryʾ /⁠čangaryā⁠/), [script needed] (cyngryʾ /⁠čingaryā⁠/), which derives perhaps from Turkic čingar.
